segments.text: American Fork City Council — Budget Workshop — February 20–21, 2025:

entities.speaker: Cameron J. Paul
entities.remark-context: Police organizational health, facilities, and operating costs

segments.text: Police Chief Cameron Paul identified organizational health, space, and increasing costs as AFPD’s three principal challenges. He discussed competition over officer wages, mental-health assistance, inadequate offices and parking, and increases since 2021 of 48% for fleet costs and 60% for fleet equipment.

entities.label: Police organizational health, space, evidence storage, and costs

segments.text: Chief Cameron Paul described the pressures affecting officer retention and wellness, as well as space, parking, vehicles, equipment, and technology. The resulting strategic plan included police/courts improvements and evidence storage at Station 52.
Relevant passages from the official meeting minutes:

Police. Chief Paul sent over the needs of the Police Department. As previously stated, personnel were important. He noted that Lehi City intends to hire ten new officers, which will affect American Fork. There are three key issues the department is facing: organizational health, space, and increased cost. The organizational health of the department is important, as they are fighting the wage battle to try to keep officers from going to other jurisdictions for more money. Mental health is also important, and they appreciate the city’s support with that. The need for mental health assistance is important, and the council felt that assistance was vital to the personnel. The police department needs space, and although they have taken over the 3rd floor of the police/courts building, they will still need to address office space and parking space. The third issue was the increased cost in fleet, general equipment, and technology. There is a 48% increase since 2021, with a 60% increase in equipment for the fleet. That increase in cost affects everything. There is new technology coming out, but that is also an added expense. They are trying to be innovative with what they do to save money.

Public Safety. The city should look at options for Station 51 expansion or temporary 53. Other items to consider are Station 53, ambulance and fire engine replacements, equipment replacement, and tenant improvements to 3rd floor of the police/courts building.

The goals for FY 2026 are:
• Public Facilities
  • Public Works
  • Fitness Center
  • Fire Station 53
  • Fire Station 51 remodel
  • Police Department remodel of 3rd floor
    • Evidence at 52
